title: BAGMAN MailboxDomainRule
description: A durable, MAILBOX-SPECIFIC sender-policy routing rule (CD-6 architect amendment — two-stage mail processing, Stage B relevance/domain gate; extended by the CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on WO into a three-state MUST_READ/GRAYLIST/BLACKLIST operator-learning model — see services.mailbox.domain_rule's own module docstring). A rule is never a global domain->entity assumption: the same sender domain may legitimately mean something different in two different mailboxes, so uniqueness/matching is always scoped to (mailbox_id, sender_domain) for a domain-level rule, or (mailbox_id, sender_address) for an EXACT_ADDRESS rule — never sender_domain/sender_address alone. A rule is always a governed, OPERATOR-APPROVED (or, for a future delivery, BAGMAN-PROPOSED-but-not-yet-approved) routing decision — never an automatic inference that mailbox == company (see services/mailbox/mailbox.py's own identical doctrine).

rule_id.description: Canonical BAGMAN identifier for this rule row.

mailbox_id.description: The `MailboxSource` this rule applies to. Rules are never shared/global across mailboxes.

sender_domain.description: The sender email domain this rule matches (for `EXACT`/`INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS`), or the domain portion of `sender_address` (for `EXACT_ADDRESS`, always kept consistent with it) — always lowercase (e.g. `vendor.com`). For a domain-level rule, canonical uniqueness is (mailbox_id, sender_domain), enforced at the repository/database layer — an operator changing their mind about a domain updates this SAME row, never creates a second one. For an `EXACT_ADDRESS` rule this field is populated purely for reporting/grouping — see `sender_address` for that rule's real identity key.

sender_address.description: CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on WO. The exact sender email address this rule matches — populated ONLY when `match_mode` is `EXACT_ADDRESS` (the real identity/uniqueness key for that match mode, scoped to (mailbox_id, sender_address)), always `null` for a domain-level (`EXACT`/`INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS`) rule.

match_mode.description: `EXACT` — only the literal `sender_domain` matches. `INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` — `sender_domain` and any subdomain of it (e.g. a rule for `vendor.com` also matches `mail.vendor.com`) matches. `EXACT_ADDRESS` (CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on WO) — only the literal `sender_address` matches, overriding any broader domain-level rule for the same domain (most-specific-rule-wins — see `services.mailbox.domain_rule.MailboxDomainRuleRepository.find_for_sender`'s own docstring). `EXACT_DOMAIN_SUBJECT` (deterministic subject-aware mailbox domain policy) — matches only a message whose sender domain EXACTLY equals `sender_domain` (never subdomains) AND whose normalised subject satisfies `subject_predicate_type`/`subject_predicate_value`. Closed, small, operator-chosen set.

policy.description: The Stage-B gate decision for mail from this sender in this mailbox (CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on WO's three-state operator-learning model — see services.mailbox.domain_rule's own module docstring for the full reasoning and the exact wire-string choice). `MUST_READ` (was `ALLOWED`) — full MIME fetch + evidence intake proceeds (subject to a per-message authentication check — see services/mailbox/sweep.py), and a later ordinary message from this SAME confirmed source never re-raises a MAILBOX_DOMAIN_REVIEW item. `GRAYLIST` (new) — Matt has looked at this domain and deliberately left it under review; behaves identically to 'no rule at all' at the Stage-B gate (bounded discovery heuristic still runs, one aggregated Needs You item is still raised/reused), the only difference being a real row now exists for GUI display. `BLACKLIST` (was `IGNORED`) — the message is observed/checked (for cursor correctness and duplicate detection) but never fetched beyond Stage-A discovery metadata, and no Needs You item is ever raised. A closed, small, real vocabulary with a real, tested, fully-reversible lifecycle transition between all three values — see `services.mailbox.domain_rule.ALLOWED_POLICY_TRANSITIONS`.

destination_entity_id.description: The canonical `GovernedEntity` this sender's evidence should route to — a real, operator-approved id, NEVER a string/name (architect spec §3). Always `null` when `policy` is `GRAYLIST` or `BLACKLIST`. May also be `null` when `policy` is `MUST_READ` and `destination_mode` is `REVIEW_REQUIRED` (domain alone cannot safely determine destination — never silently guessed).

destination_mode.description: `FIXED` — `destination_entity_id` is a confident, operator-approved routing decision. `REVIEW_REQUIRED` — this sender is a genuine accounting-evidence source but its destination entity could not be safely determined from the domain alone; evidence still gets fully ingested (per architect §5) with `entity_id` left unresolved, and a document-scoped `COMPANY_REQUIRED` Needs You item is raised per evidence item (see services/mailbox/sweep.py's own module docstring) — `destination_entity_id` stays `null` pending that per-document resolution. `null` only when `policy` is `GRAYLIST` or `BLACKLIST` (a destination concept does not apply to either).

source.description: Who/what proposed this rule. Deliberately OPEN (NOT a closed enum) per architect spec §2 — a later delivery adds a `PROPOSED_XERO_SEED` value and must never need a migration/contract change to do so. Documented (non-exhaustive) known values: `OPERATOR` (a human approved this rule directly, e.g. via a Needs You resolution), `BAGMAN_PROPOSED` (forward-declared for a future automated-proposal producer; no producer exists in this delivery).

processor_hint.description: An OPEN, free-text routing hint a human operator (or a later delivery's proposer) may attach to this rule — deliberately never a closed set of hardcoded commercial-brand-shaped values (mirrors `MailboxSource.provider_kind`'s own 'open at this layer, no hardcoded brand' doctrine one layer down). This delivery carries the field faithfully but never produces a real value for it itself.

approved_at.description: UTC timestamp this rule was last approved/set by its `source`. `null` only for a rule that has never actually been approved (not reachable by this delivery's own operator-approval-only creation path, but kept nullable for a future `BAGMAN_PROPOSED`-and-not-yet-approved row).

created_at.description: UTC timestamp this rule row was first created.

updated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent change to this row (any field).

last_seen_at.description: UTC timestamp of the most recent message this rule matched during a sweep — observability only, never itself a gate decision.

subject_predicate_type.description: Deterministic subject-aware mailbox domain policy. Populated ONLY when `match_mode` is `EXACT_DOMAIN_SUBJECT` (`null` for every other match mode — enforced at the service layer, mirrors `sender_address`'s own identical EXACT_ADDRESS-only doctrine). `EXACT` — the normalised subject must equal `subject_predicate_value` exactly. `STARTS_WITH` — the normalised subject must start with `subject_predicate_value`. No CONTAINS, no regex, no glob, no NLP — deliberately a small, deterministic, mechanically-explainable vocabulary.

subject_predicate_value.description: The predicate's own comparison value — ALWAYS stored in canonical NORMALISED form (Unicode NFKC, casefolded, stripped, internal whitespace collapsed — see `services.mailbox.domain_rule.normalize_subject_for_policy`), never raw/original casing or spacing. Populated ONLY when `match_mode` is `EXACT_DOMAIN_SUBJECT` (`null` for every other match mode — enforced at the service layer).

allOf.description: match_mode-conditional validity (CD-6 GUI-operations-foundation follow-on hardening delta) — structurally enforces, at the SCHEMA layer itself, the exact same match_mode/sender_address/subject_predicate_* correspondence `services.mailbox.domain_rule.validate_match_fields_or_raise` already enforces in Python. Defense-in-depth, not a replacement for that function: a malformed dict reaching this contract from ANY source (not only the two governed repository implementations) must be rejected here too, never merely by the domain layer above it. `EXACT_ADDRESS` is the one match_mode requiring a real `sender_address` and forbidding both subject-predicate fields — mirrors `bagman.ai_invocation.v1`'s own `role`-conditioned `allOf`/`if`/`then` style for a closed-set cross-field correspondence.

`EXACT_DOMAIN_SUBJECT` is the one match_mode requiring a real, closed-set subject predicate and forbidding `sender_address` — the schema-level mirror of `validate_match_fields_or_raise`'s own `MATCH_MODE_EXACT_DOMAIN_SUBJECT` branch. Deliberately does NOT encode subject NORMALISATION (NFKC/casefold/whitespace-collapse) here — that remains Python-only domain logic (`services.mailbox.domain_rule.normalize_subject_for_policy`); this only pins the STRUCTURAL shape (non-null, non-empty, closed predicate-type enum).

`EXACT`/`INCLUDE_SUBDOMAINS` are the two plain domain-level match modes — neither `sender_address` nor either subject-predicate field may ever be present, mirroring `validate_match_fields_or_raise`'s own final `else` branch.
